set.st: James Francis Ruggles, a Bronson rare-book dealer who died in 1911, distrusted banks after a farmhouse fire melted about $1,200 in gold. He packed $20 gold pieces into plugged iron pipes and hid several in the Ruggles Block, a building of two storeys outside and six half-floors inside, with secret panels. His brothers searched it short of tearing it down, and his brother Lon searched for months after a medium's vision; nothing was found. The block was sold to the post office in 1915. The Coldwater paper of 22 February 1915 adds that Ruggles grew up on a farm a mile west of Bronson, and that local belief put the gold inside the building he had put up, not on the farm. Pin is the post-office lot (lot 37) on the 1916 Sanborn, not a spot inside the building.
pinev: Sept 1916 Sanborn sheet 3: "POST OFFICE", two-storey brick, S side of W. Chicago St, 3rd building W of Matteson St, lot 37 (row from the corner: hardware, meat & grocery, P.O., printing).
1910 Sanborn sheet 1: the same lot 37 is labelled "Books" (Ruggles's bookshop), which had become the post office by 1915, matching the sale.
1897 and 1910 Sanborns: the post office was elsewhere, at the E end of the S-side block E of Matteson.

Building appears to survive (Street View, c.2023): a cream/white-brick two-storey with three upper windows and a red awning, third from the corner building; matched by counting from the corner, no datestone seen.
A 1939 remodel article calls it the Ruggles store building, built 1889 and the former post office, which confirms lot 37 is the Ruggles Block and that it stood in 1939.
Coldwater Daily Reporter, 22 Feb 1915: local belief kept the hoard in the block itself; the boyhood farm a mile west is background only.
